Expectation1: Look out for each other's safety and well-being
Situation1: One sibling is about to cross the street without looking for oncoming traffic.
Expectation2: Support individuals or groups in accessing essential services and resources
Situation2: They encounter a situation where someone urgently needs housing, medical help, or protection and must be connected to services quickly.
Story: I was walking with my younger brother, keeping a watchful eye on him as always, when my phone buzzed with an urgent message from the shelter. A woman and her child had just arrived, desperate for a safe place to stay and immediate medical attention. As an advocate, I knew every second counted—I needed to call the clinic, arrange transport, and make sure they weren’t turned away. But just as I started dialing, I saw my brother step off the curb, his eyes glued to his phone, oblivious to the car speeding down the street. My heart pounded. I was supposed to protect him, to make sure he was safe, but the woman on the other end of the line needed me too. I felt torn, my mind racing between shouting for my brother to stop and answering the call for help. Both needed me, right now, and I could only be in one place at a time.
